ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a circle with B as the center; A, B, C are on the same slanted straight line, and this line segment passes through the center B, so AC is a diameter. On the right there is a vertical chord EC, and point D is on EC; from B to D a horizontal line segment BD is drawn, and BD is labeled as 5x. At D there is a right-angle mark, indicating that BD is perpendicular to EC. Reasoning: Diameter AC = 20, so radius BC = 10. Because A, B, C are collinear, and C, D, E are collinear, the given angle ∠ACE = 45° corresponds to ∠BCD = 45° in right triangle BCD. In right triangle BCD, BC is the hypotenuse, length 10, and BD is the side opposite the 45° angle, therefore BD = 10 sin 45° = 10·(√2/2) = 5√2. In the figure BD is labeled 5x, so 5x = 5√2, solving gives x = √2.

raw_record.question_text: In $\odot B$, the diameter is 20 units long, and $m\angle ACE = 45$. Find $x$.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as circle centered at B, with A-B-C collinear forming the slanted diameter AC, and with BD drawn horizontally from B to the vertical chord EC; the segment BD is labeled 5x and is perpendicular to EC at D. From the text, the diameter is 20, so radius BC is 10, and angle ACE is 45°. Since A, B, C are collinear, angle ACE equals angle BCE. In right triangle BCD, BC is the radius/hypotenuse 10, angle BCD is 45°, and BD is opposite that angle. Compute BD = 10 sin 45° = 5√2. Because BD is labeled 5x, set 5x = 5√2 and get x = √2.

method.method_draft: Read the image as showing chord CE on the right side of circle B, with B the center, BC and BE radii, and BD perpendicular from the center to chord CE; BD is labeled 5x. From the text, the diameter is 20, so each radius is 10, and m∠ACE = 45°. Because A, B, C are collinear, ∠BCE = 45°. Since BC and BE are radii, triangle BCE is isosceles, so ∠CEB is also 45°, making central angle ∠CBE = 90°. Thus triangle BCE is a 45-45-90 right triangle with legs BC = BE = 10, and CE = 10√2. The perpendicular from the right-angle vertex B to hypotenuse CE has length BD = (BC·BE)/CE = 100/(10√2) = 5√2. Since BD = 5x, x = √2.

The given angle is m∠ACE = 45°.

Reasoning: Since the diameter is 20, each radius is 10, so BC = BE = 10. Because A, B, and C are collinear, ∠ACE equals ∠BCE, so ∠BCE = 45°. In triangle BCE, BC and BE are radii, so triangle BCE is isosceles, giving ∠CEB = 45° as well. Therefore ∠CBE = 180° - 45° - 45° = 90°. Since BD is labeled 5x, we have 5x = 5√2, so x = √2.
